answer: Every seat registers with a sealed tag: its operator credential, encrypted to a seven-member council so no one can read it. Think invisible pigment. When a jury flags two seats grading in lockstep, the council shines a threshold lantern on just that pair: a plaintext-equality test that reveals only same-operator or different, never a name. A match folds both seats into one payout; a miss clears them. Example: seats A and B hand 3s to the same weak answers; the test says match, so they now split one reward. Seen through this prism, clones may stay private, but never plural.
